subject: Post-call: Hyperscaler head-to-head + proposed runbook for p95/p99 tokens/sec tests
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@stratus.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + proposed runbook for p95/p99 tokens/sec tests

Team — quick recap from the call with Stratus (Alice, Tim on the line). High-level: they want an apples-to-apples latency and throughput eval against two hyperscaler-managed inference endpoints they currently run (MegaCloud Inference and HighScale AI). Their main decision criterion is 95/99 latency tail under a mixed interactive batch (short chat + 1-2 longer prompts) at target concurrent QPS. They also asked about production fallbacks and unit cost implications.

Notes:
- Stratus can provide representative traffic (we requested a 2k-sample JSONL; see attachment request).
- Their initial ask: run an A/B for 48 hours with identical payloads, report p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and per-token pricing estimate.
- They run a quantized LLM variant in HighScale and a float16 model on MegaCloud; they want to see impact of batching + KV cache across both.

Proposed next steps (please weigh in):
1) Narrow the test matrix to a succinct runbook: two model configs (float16 & int8-ish quantized) x two routing policies (direct low-latency vs cost-optimized batching) x dataset (Stratus sample + Redwood synthetic).
2) Target metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tokens/sec steady-state, tokens/sec cold-start, and cost per 1M tokens estimate.
3) Test harness: Ben to produce the JMeter-style harness that reproduces Stratus concurrent profile; Marissa to run the Redwood side A and B on Dedicated and Hosted variants.
4) Deliverable: a single CSV with per-request rows + aggregated pXX and 95% CI, plus a short slide deck with top-line differentiators.

Attachments we should prepare: runbook-diff.md, synthetic payloads, and a small script to capture KV hit/miss.

Ask: Marissa/Ben — can you draft a 1-page runbook and estimate the Redwood execution cost envelope by EOD tomorrow? Alice — can you confirm the sample payload availability and any PII redaction constraints?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment stubs: latency-raw-20261012.csv (placeholder), runbook-diff.md (outline).

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@stratus.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 17:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed runbook for p95/p99 tokens/sec tests

Jordan — thanks, captured. Draft runbook attached (short). Key clarifications I put in the doc:
- Test window: 48h steady-state + 6h warmup.
- Payload mix: 70% short (<=40 tokens), 25% medium (40-300 tokens), 5% long (>300 tokens) — matches their described traffic.
- Metrics capture: per-request latency (server and client), server token throughput, slot utilization, GPU mem/SM utilization.
- A/B definitions:
  A) Low-latency policy: small batch size (1-8), aggressive KV reuse, pinned Dedicated pool; prefer lower SLO over cost.
  B) Cost-optimized policy: larger batching (16-64), opportunistic autoscale, quantized kernels first with float fallback.

Runbook differences vs hyperscalers to highlight (short list):
- Prefix/KV caching with across-request reuse (we can show >20% p95 improvement for certain dialogs).
- Smart kernel selection per sequence length (reduces tail spikes on long sequences).
- Dedicated routing + pre-warmed pools for cold-start smoothing.

Ben — can you wire up the harness to produce the CSV schema I listed (timestamp, request_id, model_variant, routing_policy, input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_server_ms, latency_client_ms, gpu_util_pct)? If you can't get GPUs metrics from their hyperscalers we can instrument estimated token/sec from client-side timings but note limitations.

I'll also draft the one-page differentiator slide and an executive summary for Tim. Expect both by 09:00 PT tomorrow.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: runbook-diff.md (outline).

From: Alice Park <alice.park@stratus.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Huang <tim.huang@stratus.com>, procurement@stratus.com
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed runbook for p95/p99 tokens/sec tests

Thanks Jordan/Marissa — this looks good. Quick notes from Stratus: we can provide a 5k-sample file (anonymized) by EOD today; we'll strip any PII. Procurement wants a second-level cost estimate to compare to our existing contracts — not a final quote, just a run-rate +/- 10%. Tim asked specifically for p99 under a 95th-percentile concurrency point (we'll provide the exact QPS curve).

Two small asks:
1) Can you include a cold-start scenario (server restart) to show p99 spikes? That was a major customer worry after a recent incident on MegaCloud.
2) Please call out expected differences when the hyperscaler is using an int8-quantized model vs your float16 path so our infra team isn't surprised by quality vs cost tradeoffs.

We'll give you the payload and concurrency trace by 17:00 PT. If you want I'll provision a read-only API key for their endpoints so you can pull raw timings on our side (we'd prefer that to running client-side approximations).

Alice Park
Head of Platform Engineering — Stratus Systems
alice.park@stratus.com

Attachment: stratus-sample-payloads.jsonl (stub).

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@stratus.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + proposed runbook for p95/p99 tokens/sec tests

Great — appreciate the quick turnaround, Alice. We can definitely include a cold-start suite (server restart + 30 minute recovery profile) and will explicitly label model-quality/latency tradeoffs for quantized variants.

Ben/Marissa: let's lock the runbook and harness details on a 30m sync at 10:00 PT. Agenda: confirm sample ingestion, mapping of fields to CSV schema, measurement agents (client vs server), and how to securely collect hyperscaler timings if Stratus provides the read-only key. I'll invite Alice to the call.

If we can get the first draft CSV within 24 hours after the test window, we'll prepare top-line p95/p99 slides and a short cost delta analysis to show to procurement.

Thanks — JB
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
